A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 33-page versions of the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.5 support reliable comparison despite the changed title and terminology.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on WebArena, BFCLv3, and Tau-Bench, including success rates, latency measurements, and ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains those original benchmark experiments, latency measurements, and ablation results in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: The parametric and non-parametric strategies are renamed syntactic alignment (SA) and dynamics grounding (DG). The vector update/reset, persona exploration, rule extraction/filtering, and context augmentation remain unchanged. Although Figure 2 removes feedback arrows, Section 3.2 and the prompts retain on-the-fly feedback.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same WebArena websites and multi-site tasks, BFCLv3 multi-turn-base domains, and Tau-Bench airline/retail tasks. No evaluated dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 5 retain the same GPT-4.1, GPT-4o mini, Qwen2.5, WMA, hybrid, and exploration-backbone comparisons. PA/NP/NPA becoming SA/DG and shortened self-improvement labels are renamings, not comparator changes.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same splits, task counts, evaluation metrics, exploration budgets, and adaptation settings. The 30-step WebArena limit, main learning rate of 0.1 with one update, and Tau-Bench Best-of-5 simulated-user protocol are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the hybrid analysis, exploration/extractor-backbone ablation in Table 5, filtering ablation, model-size/learning-rate/update-count study in Table 6, and dynamics examples in Appendix A.5. No new analytical question or supporting experiment is introduced.

E5.justification: Both report Tau-Bench results averaged over five random seeds and retain the same discussion of evaluation variance. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or new repeated-run information.

E6.justification: The matched result entries, latency measurements, ablation scores, and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, both report GPT-4.1 WebArena success of 30.0% without DG and 35.0% with DG, and multi-site success of 2.0% and 23.0%, respectively.

T1.justification: The three deployment constraints and Equations (1)–(4) retain the same definitions and mathematical operations. Token-index typesetting changes are equivalent; no theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or removed.

C1.justification: Both retain the same two-strategy contribution, annotation-free deployment setting, efficiency claims, and benefits claimed for complex environments. The abstract drops 'complementary,' but both versions already describe mixed hybrid results and suboptimal simple combination.

C2.justification: The interpretations involving instruction-following ability, environment complexity, context length, and hybrid interference remain. Both retain limitations concerning Qwen2.5 coverage, explicit state transitions, and unnormalized adaptation updates; revised wording introduces no new applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Appendices A.1–A.3 retain the same hardware, temperatures, setup information, and prompts. Code-release and access information are unchanged. Correcting 'learning of 0.1' to 'learning rate of 0.1' clarifies an already documented setting.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to steering-vector adaptation, trained world models, and in-context memory remain unchanged. Method renaming does not introduce new related work or novelty claims.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled 'Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Agents via Environment Interaction,' adopts SA/DG terminology, corrects grammar, and clarifies several explanations. Author/header formatting changes and acknowledgments are added, while the overall section organization remains.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are recropped, and Figure 2 removes the feedback-loop arrows and corresponding caption phrase. Captions and table labels are edited, and Table 4 moves beside the latency discussion on page 8. The displays retain the same experimental data.

improvement.justification: More descriptive SA/DG terminology, grammatical corrections, and placing Table 4 beside its discussion modestly improve readability. Scientific evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged. Figure 2 becomes less explicit about feedback still described in Section 3.2, limiting the overall presentation gain.
